tldr: A known distribution of treatment benefits determines the population budget cutoff and the optimal welfare value, but it does not locate the recipients who attain that value. The object is minimax actual welfare regret on the fixed compact \(C^2\) surface orbit-closure generated by local volume-preserving transports of a public two-saddle surface, with the entire benefit distribution supplied to every procedure. A finite equal-area ranking rule is exactly feasible and attains the matched \(n^{-3/4}\log(en)\) rate against all randomized selectors in the original Bernoulli experiment. The same rate on the frozen full neighborhood is a secondary information-value comparison, not a separate primary contribution.
gap: Fixed-threshold weighted-loss bounds and mass-constrained ranking do not identify the spatial price of allocation when the complete benefit law is known. Their generic lower families need not preserve this oracle information.
fill: A transported spatial converse and an exactly feasible finite ranking upper bound determine whether critical contour geometry imposes a regret logarithm even after all distributional uncertainty is removed.
